statement: The Juggler-Collatz bridge, stated as theorems over the one shared object, the List Branch word, with no real number and nothing measured in any statement. COLLATZ IS WORD-AFFINE WITH THE CORRECTION POINTING UP: for the shortcut map C (x/2 on evens, (3x+1)/2 on odds) and w = parityWord x d the first d parities of the orbit of x, 2^d * C^d(x) = 3^(oddCount w) * x + wordConst w with wordConst w >= 0 a function of the word alone (word_affine; wordConst (odd :: w) = 3^(oddCount w) + 2 wordConst w, wordConst (even :: w) = 2 wordConst w, and wordConst w = 0 iff w has no odd letter). JUGGLER IS EXPONENT-AFFINE WITH THE CORRECTION POINTING DOWN: juggler_word_power restates power_bound_word as (image n w)^(2^|w|) <= n^(3^(oddCount w)) for a realised word. The same multiplier 3^o/2^d acts on x in one problem and on log n in the other, with corrections of opposite sign, and that is the whole of the sign flip on cycles: cycle_contracting (a positive shortcut cycle of length d >= 1 has 3^o < 2^d, because 2^d x = 3^o x + c with c >= 1 whenever the word has an odd letter and 2^d x = x is impossible otherwise) sits beside juggler_cycle_expanding = cycle_itinerary_formally_expanding (2^d < 3^o). TERRAS IN THIS VOCABULARY: parityWord_eq_iff, parityWord x d = parityWord y d iff x = y mod 2^d, and image_parityWord, the residues modulo 2^d map bijectively onto allWords d (allWords_card gives 2^d). Compiles with no sorry; #print axioms on word_affine gives propext and Quot.sound only, on the counting theorems propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Registered as an auxiliary Juggler module (not a paper review object); it imports Problems.Collatz.Shortcut, RateFreeDensity, PaperBCertificateRecursion, Envelope and CycleCore. WHAT IT IS NOT: no density, no asymptotic, no bound in either problem, and nothing about how the Juggler word attaches to n, which is Hypothesis FD. It records that the bridge of J-juggler-is-collatz-one-exponential-up is well defined at the word level, and it closes the gap that the Collatz half of the sign flip was previously only an algebraic lemma with the orbit identity assumed (Problems/Collatz/Cycles.lean expanding_excludes_positive_candidate): the identity is now derived by iterating shortcutC. Process note: the module was swept into commit 4c078205 by a concurrent session's git add -A before its own record existed; the build was then verified by that session (lake build Problems.Juggler, 8909 jobs) and here. NOTE 2026-09-19: CollatzBridge.lean now defines the shortcut map locally and is a layer module of Paper A's barrel; decidedAtResidues_card and neg_seventeen_inhabits_cycleMinShape live in the auxiliary CollatzBridgeLab.lean, same namespace, outside the barrel.

The family of all minimal exponent-descent certificate words is prefix-free: if two certificates are in the prefix relation, they are equal. Grouping by positive word length, its fair mass has sum one: HasSum certMass 1, where certMass d=M_(d+1)/2^(d+1). This follows from the exact partition sum_(d<D) certMass d+N_D/2^D=1 and the existing unconditional word-survivor decay. Its tilted mass, the sum of 2^(-|w|)*rho_w with rho_w=3^(oddCount w)/2^|w|, is summable and at most 3/4, hence not one. Every terminal multiplier is below one; the certificate E has fair mass 1/2 but tilted mass 1/4, and the remaining fair mass is 1/2. Thus Kraft completeness alone does not justify the first multiplier-moment identity at unbounded stopping. This is a counterexample to the former unrestricted second-root sentence in Paper C Section 5.7, not to its coefficient shift, Proposition 5.12, or a termination theorem. The compiled theorem complete_family_moment_loss packages the prefix-free property and both sums. Ledger label awaits advisory coverage review.

The direct Walsh estimate of the good set is refuted, and it refutes the reading of Proposition J's loss recorded a day earlier. THE MEASUREMENT. Expanding the good-set indicator in Walsh characters gives S(N,d) = sum_S ghat(S) W_S(N) with main term ghat(0) N = (N_d/2^d) N, so the gain over Proposition J's union bound would be N_d / ||ghat||_1. Parseval gives sum_S ghat(S)^2 = N_d/2^d and hence ||ghat||_1 <= sqrt(N_d) unconditionally, so gamma <= sqrt(2 theta) = 1.389897 is a THEOREM and the 'fully direct' reading with gamma = 1 was never available. Measured, gamma SATURATES that ceiling. Four independent computations agree -- a numpy FWHT to d = 29, a factored transform to d = 40, exact Fractions and brute-force summation from the definition at small d, and a Monte-Carlo extension to d = 386 -- and all reproduce the exact values 2.90625, 6.316406, 17.114990, 44.315536, 61.052952 at d = 8, 12, 16, 20, 22. The naive fitted exponent drifts UPWARD with the window, 1.28344 at d = 14..22 to 1.31824 at d = 26..34 to 1.335 at d = 30..38, toward 1.389897 and not away from it; the same naive estimator applied to sqrt(N_d), whose rate is known exactly, is itself biased low by two percent, and a three-parameter fit returns gamma = 1.394 to 1.424, at or just over the rigorous ceiling. So the earlier reading of 1.28 to 1.30 as a limit below Parseval was the drifting-exponent trap for the fourth time in a week. THE STRUCTURE IS REAL BUT POLYNOMIAL: ||ghat_d||_1 ~ Phi(frac(d beta)) sqrt(N_d) d^(-0.83), the exact structural analogue of N_d/2^d ~ psi(frac(d beta)) theta^d d^(-3/2), with Phi discontinuous at frac = beta -- the same jump location as psi. A polynomial factor does not move an exponential rate, so the best the route could give is the Parseval 1.90x. AND EVEN THAT IS NOT AVAILABLE, which is the decisive point. The two bases are related by exact identities in each direction: W_S(N) = sum_w (-1)^(w.S)(#w(N) - 2^-d N) gives max_S |W_S| <= 2^d E_d, and #w(N) - 2^-d N = 2^-d sum_(S != 0) (-1)^(w.S) W_S gives E_d <= max_(S != 0)|W_S|. Both ends are attained. A Walsh estimate needs max|W_S| to be comparable to E_d; Proposition J's hypothesis supplies only the reverse, so the conversion costs 2^d and the route is WORSE by 2^d ||ghat||_1/N_d -- measured 114x at d = 12, 531x at d = 16, 1700x at d = 20, 8199x at d = 24, growing like 1.44^d. Seen properly, Paper B's identity (2.1) is ITSELF a Walsh expansion, in the (w,A) formal-chain basis, with every coefficient +/- 2^(-(d-1)) and Wiener norm exactly N_d(1 - 2^(-(d-1))): the union bound is the L1 bound in the only basis the hypothesis controls, and it is termwise sharp there. The 1.90x returns only if Hypothesis FD is restated as a uniform character bound max_(S != 0)|W_S(N)| <= B, which is not what the laboratory's machinery proves -- that machinery controls formal-chain correlations R_(w,A) for a fixed word w, and (-1)^(x_k(n)) agrees with the formal sign only on the cell where the orbit follows w.

The Wiener norm of the good set carries the rotation, like everything else in this cluster. ||ghat_d||_1 ~ Phi(frac(d beta)) sqrt(N_d) d^(-0.83), the structural analogue of N_d/2^d ~ psi(frac(d beta)) theta^d d^(-3/2), with Phi a function of the rotation coordinate alone -- a collapse test gives 4.7 percent scatter over d = 10..38 -- and discontinuous at frac = beta, the same jump location as psi. THE PLATEAUS ARE EXACT AND HAVE A ONE-LINE PROOF. If step d is free, meaning ceil(d beta) = ceil((d-1) beta), then every good word of length d-1 extends by both bits, so Good_d = Good_(d-1) x {0,1} and ghat_d(S,0) = ghat_(d-1)(S) while ghat_d(S,1) = 0. Hence ||ghat_d||_1 = ||ghat_(d-1)||_1 EXACTLY while N_d = 2 N_(d-1). That accounts for the repeated values in the data, with one exception worth keeping: d = 5 is NOT free -- N_5 = 4 against 2 N_4 = 6 -- yet the norm does not move there either, so a plateau is evidence of a free step and not proof of one. The lemma is the empty-window theorem of PaperBCertificateLengths acting on the spectrum rather than on the counts, the third place this week that theorem has turned up controlling something new. Consequence for measurement: fit the Wiener norm per RISE, not per depth, because the free steps contribute exactly zero and a per-depth fit is modulated by the Sturmian word. Rigorous bounds: 1 <= ||ghat_d||_1 <= sqrt(N_d), the upper by Cauchy-Schwarz and Parseval, the lower because max_S |ghat(S)| = ghat(0) for a non-negative indicator. That gamma equals the upper end rather than lying strictly below it is measured, not proved; a matching lower bound ||ghat_d||_1 >= sqrt(N_d)/poly(d) would close it.

Juggler is Collatz one exponential level up, and that is why the survivor counts coincide. Accelerated Collatz sends x to x/2 or (3x+1)/2, so log x moves by -log 2 or +log(3/2). Juggler sends n to floor(sqrt n) or floor(n^(3/2)), so log n is MULTIPLIED by 1/2 or 3/2 and therefore log log n moves by -log 2 or +log(3/2). The same additive walk with the same two steps, carried on log x in one problem and on log log n in the other. Measured from the seed 10^20 + 1 the Juggler increments are +0.405465108108 and -0.693147180560 against those targets, agreeing to 2e-16; at n = 7 the same increments are wrong by a percent, because the floor costs O(1) in n and so O(1/n) in log n. HENCE ONE COUNT. After m steps with o odd the walk sits at o log 3 - m log 2, and 'has not dropped below the start' is 3^o >= 2^m in both problems, so the non-contracting words are the same words and N_d is the same integer. Checked by running Collatz rather than by quoting OEIS: for d = 4 to 10 the parity map is bijective on Z/2^d and the number of residue classes whose stopping time is not constant is 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 38, 64, exactly N_d. WHERE THEY PART, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF PAPER B. For Collatz the parity word is a function of x mod 2^d and the map onto {0,1}^d is a bijection, so every word has density exactly 2^(-d) -- Terras, arithmetic and free. For Juggler the word is a function of frac(n^(3/2)) and its relatives, and equal densities are Hypothesis FD, which is open and is the analytic burden of the paper. Same combinatorics, incompatible arithmetic. CONSEQUENCES. The asymptotic of J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence is unconditional for Collatz and conditional for Juggler, since Terras supplies there what FD only conjectures here. Collatz is a free validator for any FD-conditional derivation that depends only on word densities, because there such a statement is a theorem and a failure would indict the derivation rather than FD. WHAT IT IS NOT. Not an equivalence and not a conjugacy: the maps are not conjugate, only the multiplier semigroup is one. It moves no bound in either problem and proves nothing new about Collatz beyond restating Terras. Juggler is not an easier Collatz -- it is Collatz's word problem plus a Weyl-sum problem, and both stall at the same wall. Its value is as a separator: it keeps the combinatorics and removes the 2-adic rigidity, so it shows which parts of Collatz need the 2-adics and which need only the words. Distinct from the killed BT warp W as a conjugacy and from reversal as a Collatz intertwiner, which concern a numeration system rather than the semigroup.

There is a code H from all natural Juggler starts to the 2-adic integers, constructed from compatible finite Collatz residues with no termination hypothesis. Its residue modulo two has the parity of the start. It satisfies H(J(n))=minusStep(H(n)) and -H(J(n))=plusStep(-H(n)), where the steps are the 2-adic 3n-1 and 3n+1 shortcut maps, and H(J^d(n))=minusStep^d(H(n)) for every d. For all natural r,d, H(n)=-r modulo 2^d if and only if the actual length-d Juggler itinerary of n equals the length-d 3n+1 itinerary of r. Consequently these conditions select exactly the same subset of any finite source set; no equidistribution estimate is asserted. On each start with a ReachesOne witness, H agrees in the 2-adic field with the previously defined rational terminatingCode. This is classical parity coding, not ordinary-integer transport or universal termination. The local Lean proof is compiled; the ledger label awaits advisory coverage review.

For every natural n and L>0 with J^L(n)=n, put w=itinerary(n,L), A=wordConst(w), and D=3^oddCount(w)-2^L as a signed integer. Then D is nonzero and the global 2-adic code H(n) equals the rational A/D in the 2-adic field. The least periods of H(n) under the 3n-1 map and of -H(n) under the 3n+1 map both equal the least Juggler period of n. H(n) is an embedded ordinary integer if and only if D divides A. If H(n)=z for an integer z, then for every d the ordinary integer 3n+1 shortcut returns -z after d steps if and only if Juggler returns n after d steps. Period preservation follows from branch monotonicity on equal-code fibers; global injectivity is not assumed. This proves no word divisibility for actual Juggler cycles and excludes no new cycle. Local Lean compilation is complete; ledger retagging awaits advisory coverage review.

For each finite parity word w, define p_w=2^(-|w|), rho_w=3^(oddCount w)/2^|w|, and c_w=3^(-oddCount w). For every real s, c_w*rho_w^s=p_w*rho_w^(s-1). At every fixed depth d, summing over all binary words of length d gives sum p_w=1 and sum p_w*rho_w=1. The fair and tilted child weights each sum to their parent's weight, so finite leaf expansions preserve both totals. These are word identities, not arithmetic counting estimates for Juggler starts. Correction of 22 September 2026: the previous complete-prefix-free wording did not distinguish bounded trees from unbounded stopping. Completeness alone does not preserve the second moment identity: J-collatz-complete-stopping-loses-moment supplies a kernel-checked counterexample. The coefficient shift and Proposition 5.12's ideal-model root at one remain valid. The stale attribution of the entire gap to a parity shortfall is removed: Paper C's printed individual coefficients already equal the ideal, while overlap and truncation affect their assembly. Compiled declarations and an 18-declaration dependency audit are recorded; the ledger tag awaits advisory coverage review.

The analogue of Paper C Theorem 1 for every nonempty backward-closed set is false for both ordinary Collatz shortcut signs. For C_plus(n)=n/2 on evens and (3n+1)/2 on odds, and C_minus(n)=n/2 on evens and (3n-1)/2 on odds, every multiple m of three has exactly the one predecessor 2m. Consequently A={3*2^k : k>=0} is infinite and backward-closed for both maps. Its injective geometric enumeration has reciprocal sum exactly 2/3, and every finite subset S of A has sum_{n in S} 1/n <= 2/3. The ray is not forward-closed: C_plus(3)=5 and C_minus(3)=4 leave it. It therefore does not itself refute a fate-specific almost-all-to-all implication. This is the exact obstruction to transferring the general backward-density engine, not a termination or nontermination result. The shortcut convention is explicit; acceleratedT elsewhere in the repository is the distinct odd-only map. The local Lean proof is compiled; ledger retagging awaits advisory coverage review.

The useful comparison is worst-case backward harmonic mass. For Juggler, the mass M_J(m) of the even block [m^2,(m+1)^2) satisfies m/(m+1)^2 <= M_J(m) <= (m+1)/m^2 for every positive m, so m*M_J(m) tends to one. It is not exactly 1/m and need not exceed 1/m: M_J(3)=107/420<1/3. The lower bound is the existing kernel-checked evenBlock_logMass_ge in FateSeed.lean; the current Paper C manuscript already uses its valid consequence (1-2/m)/m. For the ordinary 3n+1 shortcut map, the normalized predecessor mass is exactly 1/2 on m not congruent to 2 modulo 3, and 1/2+3m/(2m-1) on the remaining residue. Its arithmetic mean tends to one, but no finite mean is asserted to equal one. The census through 20000 gives approximately 1.000185. Every multiple of three has exact mass 1/(2m), and the ray {3*2^k} realizes that loss forever for both signs, as formalized in J-paper-c-collatz-analogue-is-false-by-exhibit. Correction of 22 September 2026: the former exact-equality and never-below claims were false; the regression had sampled only even Juggler targets. Both target parities and exact rational counterexamples are now tested. The finite census remains computational; no termination bound changes.

WITHDRAWN THE FOLLOWING DAY. This row claimed that Proposition J's loss is the union bound rather than the exponent, and that combining the word classes better was worth about twenty times against 1.33 for improving delta. The arithmetic of the comparison is right and the conclusion is wrong, for two independent reasons, either of which is fatal. FIRST, the 20x reading required ||ghat||_1 = O(1) and the Wiener norm of the good set saturates the Parseval ceiling, gamma = sqrt(2 theta), measured to d = 386 by four independent methods; the best the route could ever give is the 1.90x. SECOND and decisively, even the 1.90x is not available under the hypothesis this row was written about. Proposition J supplies a per-word error E_d, and a Walsh estimate needs a character bound; the exact identities give E_d <= max_(S != 0)|W_S| <= 2^d E_d with both ends attained, so the conversion costs 2^d and the route is worse by 114x at d = 12 rising to 8199x at d = 24. Paper B's identity (2.1) is itself a Walsh expansion in the (w,A) formal-chain basis with Wiener norm exactly N_d(1 - 2^(-(d-1))): the union bound IS the L1 bound in the only basis the hypothesis controls, and it is termwise sharp there, so calling it a loss was the error. WHAT SURVIVES: the density-exponent arithmetic itself, which is correct and is kept in J-proposition-j-on-collatz-is-terras; and the observation that a character-form hypothesis max_(S != 0)|W_S(N)| <= B would give the 1.90x, which is a statement about a hypothesis the laboratory does not have. Full account in J-good-set-walsh-route-is-refuted.

Proposition J applied to Collatz is Terras 1976, and that calibrates what Hypothesis FD is worth. J-equidistribution-implies-density-one bounds the starts with no contracting prefix of length at most d by (N_d/2^d) N + N_d E_d(N). On the Collatz side Terras makes the parity map a bijection on Z/2^d, so a word class holds floor(N/2^d) or ceil(N/2^d) integers and E_d(N) = O(1): the usable depth is log2 N and the non-descending starts are N^(1 - 0.050044). That is the quantitative form of the density-one stopping-time theorem. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED 19 September 2026 by the priority reading (J-paper-b-survivors-are-oeis-a076227): the MECHANISM is Terras 1976 and this row's title stands -- the parity bijection on Z/2^d, hence E_d(N) = O(1), hence density one, is his, jointly with Everett 1977. THE EXPONENT IS NOT. The 0.050044 enters through N_d/2^d <= theta^d, and that bound is Lagarias 1985, Theorem D: 1 - F(k) <= 2^(-eta k) with eta = 1 - H((log_2 3)^(-1)) = 0.050044472811669365186, H the binary entropy function, proved there from Terras's structure by a binomial tail and sharpened two-sidedly in the remark after it. Theorem D carries no attribution label in the survey although its Theorems A and C are both labelled (Terras), and Lagarias's own annotated bibliography credits Terras 1976 with the residue-class structure, the coefficient stopping time and natural density one, and with no rate. So 'known since 1976' is right for the density and wrong for the exponent, which is known since 1985. CAVEAT: Terras 1976 itself could not be read -- the matwbn scan sits behind an anti-bot gate -- so this correction rests on Lagarias's annotation of Terras rather than on Terras's text, and would be overturned by an exponential estimate inside the 1976 paper. THE CONVERSION. Minimising the two terms over d turns an equidistribution exponent into a density exponent. With FD at power saving delta, E_d(N) = O(N^(1-delta)), the error beats the main term once 2^d exceeds N^delta, so the usable depth is delta log2 N and the density exponent is delta times Collatz's: exactly 0.050044 delta. Juggler's conditional result is therefore a delta-fraction of Collatz's unconditional one, and reaching parity needs delta = 1, meaning bounded error per class. No Weyl-type discrepancy bound for frac(n^(3/2)) gives O(1); that is what a bijection gives and an equidistribution estimate does not. A CAVEAT ADDED THE NEXT DAY: no stated conclusion of Paper B consumes this exponent. Theorem 6.1 fixes d, sends N to infinity and only then lets d grow, so N_d is constant during the limit that matters and N_d E_d(N) = o(N) comes free; the manuscript says its conclusion follows from any theta < 1, Hypothesis FD is stated with no common error rate in d assumed, and J-rate-free-density-one records that the qualitative conclusion survives rate-free. The conversion below is therefore a calibration of what FD would be worth, not a target to optimise. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROADMAP. If FD were proved outright, Juggler would arrive exactly where Collatz has been for fifty years, and no further -- Collatz has had the density-one theorem since 1976, and its quantitative form since 1985, and termination is still open. FD is a hard analytic theorem in a setting with no arithmetic, and worth wanting on those terms; it is not a step toward termination. TWO CORRECTIONS, from a review by balanced-ternary-e3. The exponent this row originally quoted, delta = 1/96, is the 4 September target that Paper B withdrew; the ledger retains 95/96 only as a historical research target. What the current paper proves is delta = 1/24 at four steps and 1/128 at five. And the power-saving hypothesis is Conjecture K, not Hypothesis FD -- FD is stated with no common error rate in d assumed and so carries no delta at all; saying 'FD with power saving delta' conflated the two. At the proved exponents the union-bound bound is N^0.997915 at delta = 1/24 and N^0.999609 at 1/128, and reaching even N^0.99 by this route would need delta above 1/5 -- a factor of five beyond the depth-four exponent, not the factor of nineteen this row first reported against the withdrawn one.

For every natural n with a witness h that its actual Juggler orbit reaches 1, terminatingCode n h is a positive rational number independent of the chosen hitting time: whenever J^d(n)=1 it equals codeAt n d, the inverse 3n-1 branch composition along itinerary n d applied to endpoint 1. At every such depth d its reduced denominator divides 3^oddCount(itinerary n d). Its denominator is odd and its reduced numerator has the same parity as n. Writing H for this code on the terminating basin, H(J(n))=minusStep(H(n)) and -H(J(n))=plusStep(-H(n)), where minusStep and plusStep select their rational shortcut branch using reduced-numerator parity. This is a theorem on the terminating basin only; it does not define the full infinite 2-adic code or assert universal termination or ordinary-integer transport.

Paper B's survivor count is a Collatz residue count, in Lean. undecidedResidues_card: the number of residues r modulo 2^d whose parity word parityWord r d has no contracting prefix equals neverNegCount d, the N_d of RateFreeDensity; decidedAtResidues_card: the number whose word is a minimal certificate (first contracts at exactly d) equals minimalCertCount d, the M_d of PaperBCertificateRecursion. Both follow from Terras's bijection (image_parityWord) by pushing the filter through the image. THE COLLATZ MEANING IS MADE EXACT, with Terras's 'all sufficiently large' threshold explicit: le_iter_of_prefixNoncontracting, no member of an undecided class drops within d steps (x <= C^t(x) for t <= d, strictly for x >= 1 and t >= 1); iter_lt_of_exponentGap_class, every member y of a decided class with y > wordConst (parityWord r t) drops at the contracting length t (C^t(y) < y) -- so a class is undecided iff no member drops, and decided iff all but finitely many members drop at the same step, which is OEIS A076227's definition ('residue classes in which the stopping time is not constant') read at large members; at x = 1 the literal reading differs (sigma(1) is infinite in the class of 1 mod 4, whose word OE contracts), and the Lean statement is the word criterion with the threshold, not the literal one. KERNEL CHECKS: undecidedResidues 6 = {7, 15, 27, 31, 39, 47, 59, 63}, the entry's own example (Labos Elemer, 2002), and (undecidedResidues d).card = 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 38, 64 for d = 4..10, all by decide +kernel (the depth-10 check runs 1024 residues through ten shortcut steps in the kernel). UPGRADE: the count half of J-juggler-is-collatz-one-exponential-up and of J-paper-b-survivors-are-oeis-a076227 was COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED by running Collatz on eight sampled lifts per class for d = 4..10 (a check that is exact at those depths by exhaustive comparison but not sound by construction); it is now a theorem for every d. Through this row the word-only modules PaperBCertificateRecursion, PaperBCertificateLengths, PaperBJumpTransposition and PaperBSurvivorDecay are theorems about Collatz residue classes as well: the recursion N_(d+1) + M_(d+1) = 2 N_d is OEIS A076227's Zarubin 2019 formula, the empty-window theorem is Noe's 2006 comment on A100982 (lengths are A020914(k), the binary length of 3^k), and the stepFlat/stepRise profile is Winkler's 2017 Pascal-type triangle -- all KNOWN as formulas, kernel-verified here for the first time as far as the laboratory has read. Not a density, not a bound, not a halt theorem. NOTE 2026-09-19: CollatzBridge.lean now defines the shortcut map locally and is a layer module of Paper A's barrel; decidedAtResidues_card and neg_seventeen_inhabits_cycleMinShape live in the auxiliary CollatzBridgeLab.lean, same namespace, outside the barrel.

A Collatz-side import checked on the laboratory's own counts. Winkler (OEIS A100982 comment, 15 September 2026; preprint 'Admissible qx+1 Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers') states, with alpha = log2 3 and m_n = floor(n alpha): (1/n) C(m_n - 1, n - 1) <= a(n) <= (1/n) C(m_n, n - 1), with equality in the lower bound exactly when {n alpha} is a strict record minimum among {j alpha}, 1 <= j <= n, and in the upper bound exactly when it is a strict record maximum -- the equality orders being the denominators of the one-sided convergents and semiconvergents of log2 3, where a(n) is a rational Catalan number. The laboratory's minimal-certificate count M_d = 2 N_{d-1} - N_d (PaperBCertificateRecursion; N_d from survivor_counts) equals A100982(n) at d = A020914(n) = the binary length of 3^n, and vanishes at every other length (the empty-window theorem, PaperBCertificateLengths; checked for d <= 3508: the nonzero lengths are exactly A020914(k), k >= 0, 2214 of them). On those counts the sandwich holds for every order n = 1..2213, the head is 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 12, 30, 85, 173, 476, 961, 2652 as in A100982, lower equality holds at n = 2, 7, 12, 53, 359, 665 (the record minima) and upper equality at n = 3, 5, 17, 29, 41, 94, 147, 200, 253, 306, 971, 1636 (the record maxima), both lists matching Winkler's characterisation with n = 1 the degenerate common case. WHAT THIS SAYS FOR THE BRIDGE. It is an independent 2026 confirmation, from the Collatz literature, of the Sturmian structure the laboratory reads on the same words: the extremal orders of M are the one-sided convergents, the coordinate is {n log2 3}, and the jump locations of J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence sit on the same rotation orbit. Winkler's bounds pin M_n to within the ratio C(m_n, n-1)/C(m_n - 1, n-1) = m_n/(m_n - n + 1) about 2.7, so they neither give nor contradict the d^(-3/2) or the oscillating prefactor; that remains Hikawa's Conjecture 7.1 and the laboratory's measurement. KNOWN (Winkler); the check is the laboratory's. Not a density, not a bound on any Juggler orbit. CORRECTION 2026-09-19: the row records only the sandwich, and that preprint also claims more. Its abstract closes 'We also prove monotonicity in q, compare the three OEIS sequences, and derive their growth constants and exact normalized oscillations', for A100982, A174795 and A174796. The laboratory's psi is the prefactor of the SURVIVOR count A076227 and Winkler's oscillations are for the minimal-certificate count A100982, which is M_d; the two are tied by M_d = 2 N_{d-1} - N_d, so whether his result determines psi is a question about that identity and not an open one. The paper's theorems have not been read here, only the abstract. This bears directly on the one thing Paper B offers on its own account, so the novelty gate on psi is NOT clear.
